requirements.text: open a high-impact, high-urgency incident describing the freezing and dropped-call issue
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_024' AND caller_id = 'USER_006' AND configuration_item = 'CI_005' AND status = 'new' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_024 after INC_023); the only incident the task creates
caller is Elena Petrov, 'the contact for this device', resolved to USER_006 in the seed (also the CI's owner_id)
the incident is linked to the hub itself (configuration_item = CI_005): the benchmark check joins on its serial, here the id is used directly; CI_005 is in_use so policy 5.1 allows the link
priority critical from the policy's impact x urgency matrix (high, high)
status new: the policy's default for new incidents; kept from the benchmark check
the freezing and dropped-call wording is free text and is not tested; the benchmark check does not test it either

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on every requirement, value and disposition: the cost change on CI_005 and the critical incident INC_024 for Elena on the hub, both benchmark checks kept; no disagreements. No stay requirements: the serial matches exactly one CI, the request forbids nothing, and other CIs' costs are a generic invariant the collateral audit measures. No knowledge article in the seed relates to video conferencing (the five cover passwords, Outlook, desktop boot and email access), so policy 7's suggested-link rule adds no requirement, and no listed tool searches or links knowledge. No tool writes incident_affected_cis; the CI link is tested on incident.configuration_item as the benchmark does. The hub sits at LOC_003 (San Francisco) under ORG_002 while Elena is in ORG_001; neither org_id nor location is fixed by the request, so neither is a cell. The serial's LON tag against the San Francisco location is odd but not acted on.
